claim: In March 2026, the Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS) bought four Chevrolet Tahoes fitted out as covert surveillance vans for about $4.5 million — the largest US sale on record for the Israeli surveillance firm Cognyte, a 2021 spinoff of Verint that markets itself as a rival to Palantir. Each van carries FalcoNet, a cell-site simulator (an "IMSI catcher," the kind of device also known as a Stingray): it "simulates a mobile phone tower, which forces nearby phones to connect to it," letting police pull identifying data off every device in range — suspect or not — and, per Cognyte's own materials, force thousands of devices to connect per minute. Cognyte has sold the same technology to other US agencies: the Albuquerque, New Mexico police, the New York State Police, and the Florida Department of Law Enforcement, which spent $765,000 on FalcoNet in 2024 for a Caribbean mass-migration operation. Cognyte's US revenue rose from $10 million in 2023 to $15 million in 2025.

sources.label: Forbes — Thomas Brewster, "Israel's Palantir Rival Is Selling $1 Million Spy Vans To U.S. Cops" (July 13, 2026). The Texas deal, FalcoNet, Cognyte, and the other US buyers.
